answer.reason: Genesis 4 tells of Cain's offering, the killing of Abel, and his banishment and city-building, though the killing is already named in the summary only as a relation, so it can be told once as a deed.

clauses.english: brought an offering of the fruit of the ground, which the LORD did not accept
clauses.quote: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.

clauses.english: rose up against his brother Abel in the field and slew him
clauses.quote: Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

clauses.english: was marked by the LORD so that no one finding him would kill him
clauses.quote: the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

clauses.english: built a city and named it after his son Enoch
clauses.quote: he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.

doubts: Four clauses chosen for a life told in one chapter; the offering and the mark could be dropped if the line runs long.
Left out HEB 11:4, 1JN 3:12 and JUD 1:11 as comment on Cain rather than new events; GEN 4:24 is Lamech's boast, not a deed of Cain.
